result.title: Rethinking Video Agents: When and Why Video Harnesses Work
result.summary: Video understanding depends not only on how models reason about visual evidence, but also on which evidence they observe. Fixed observation policies determine this evidence in advance; agentic harnesses allow models to seek further observations as their understanding develops. This shift creates an opportunity to realize capabilities that fixed inputs leave untapped, yet the ability to request observations does not ensure their effective use. We investigate when and why video harnesses improve understanding, examining how task demands and models' capacity for interaction jointly shape their benefits. Using Video-Relook as an experimental framework, we let models adapt their temporal and spatial observations from a common default configuration, and analyze performance and interaction trajectories across models and tasks. Adaptive observation yields substantial gains on fine-grained action understanding, with benefits also extending to Video-MME-v2. Even under the same observation interface, gains differ substantially across models; interaction traces reveal corresponding differences in evidence seeking and the reliability of answer revision. The benefits also vary across tasks for the same model, ranging from substantial improvements to limited gains and regressions. Together, these findings support an account in which harness effectiveness depends on the alignment between opportunities for informative observation and the model's ability to turn interaction into reliable revisions. They motivate video harnesses that coordinate perception and reasoning, matching observational autonomy to task demands and model capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以 Video-Relook 为实验框架，让模型从统一默认配置出发自适应调整时间与空间观察范围，分析不同模型与任务下自适应观察的性能变化及交互轨迹，并总结 harness 生效取决于「信息性观察机会」与「模型将交互转化为可靠修订的能力」之间的匹配。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「何时 LOOK、获取何种视觉证据」及收益–成本问题，其模型间证据寻求与答案修订差异可供核查 LOOK/STOP 收益对模型能力和任务需求的依赖；但机制是视频 agent 的外部观察接口，而非 latent 状态生成。
